objective: Proof and computation. When the hub of the removed line and one near point pin the gluing line's pattern, does the hub reach the ports through a single port class: tied to a port other than the pinned pattern's odd port, or in a near knot with the two other ports whose excluded pattern is one step from the pinned one? Test on plane and non-planar near sides. Prove that the hub's tie class contains every point on the removed line's faces, and that the lemma gives an elimination route for every pinned-and-separated three-point knot whatever the far side.
status: Proved by PLANAR-COMPOSE-20261102-001A-P001: on a plane near side the hub's tie class contains every point on the removed line's faces (matching cycles flip what they enclose and never enter those faces); route lemma (a pinning with the hub tied to a non-odd port, or in a two-port near knot pointing one step from the pinned pattern, generates every pinned-and-separated three-point knot for any far side); access lemma checked on 30 plane spaces (4560 pinnings) and failing on every pinning of the Fano plane and census 58 (336); so no such knot is new on these plane sides whatever the far side; open: the access lemma in general
title: The hub reaches the ports on a plane side
